report.incidentSummary: At market open (09:15 IST / 03:45 UTC on 2026-09-14), stock orders experienced a ~15.5% failure rate lasting until ~04:21 UTC (09:51 IST). Concurrently, primary database CPU spiked from ~35% to ~77%. Investigation confirmed that order rejections were directly caused by upstream broker API rate limiting (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests due to exceeding the 300 req/s threshold), which caused order-service to exhaust its retries and return HTTP 503. The concurrent database CPU spike was an independent side effect of market-open portfolio traffic running unindexed holdings queries and did not cause database pool exhaustion or order timeouts.
report.rootCauseStatement: Surging market-open order placement traffic exceeded upstream broker-api's rate limit quota of 300 requests/second. Upstream broker-api responded with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests), causing broker-connector to fail order submissions and order-service to exhaust its retry budget, rejecting approximately 15% of customer orders with HTTP 503.

hypotheses.cause: Market-open order volume exceeded the external broker API rate limit of 300 req/s. Upstream broker-api returned HTTP 429 responses to broker-connector, causing order-service to exhaust retries and reject orders with HTTP 503.
hypotheses.rationale: Direct error logs in broker-connector and order-service demonstrate repeated HTTP 429 responses from broker-api citing a 300 req/s limit starting at 03:45:05 UTC, exactly coinciding with the surge in error rates across both services until 04:21 UTC.

hypotheses.cause: Market-open user traffic triggered unindexed holdings queries on database, saturating database CPU to ~77% and degrading order-service database transactions.
hypotheses.rationale: Although database CPU spiked to ~77% due to slow queries on the holdings table, database connection pool wait times in order-service remained minimal (peaking at only 5.14 ms), lock wait times remained steady (~4 ms), and order-service logs contained zero database timeout or connection exhaustion errors.

facts.statement: order-service error_rate jumped from a baseline of ~0.3-0.5% to ~15.5% between 03:46 UTC and 04:17 UTC (peaking at 15.62% at 04:03 UTC) before returning to baseline by 04:21 UTC.
broker-connector error_rate spiked from ~0.2% to ~11.3% between 03:46 UTC and 04:17 UTC (peaking at 11.34% at 03:48 UTC) before returning to baseline by 04:21 UTC.
broker-connector logged 378 occurrences of 'POST /orders -> 429 Too Many Requests (limit 300 req/s; retry-after 1s)' from upstream broker-api between 03:45:05 UTC and 04:20:59 UTC.
order-service logged 290 occurrences of 'order <ref> rejected: broker rate limit (429) after 2 retries' returning status 503 between 03:45:32 UTC and 04:21:29 UTC.
order-service db_pool_wait_ms remained between 2.2 ms and 5.14 ms throughout the window.
Database db_lock_wait_ms remained between 3.5 ms and 4.5 ms and active_connections remained steady around ~175 connections without connection spikes.

Database cpu_utilization jumped from ~35% to 50.37% at 03:45 UTC and remained elevated at 72-77% until ~04:30 UTC, coinciding with slow queries (1100-3200 ms) executing 'SELECT ... FROM holdings WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY updated_at'.
No deployments, migrations, or config changes occurred on order-service, database, or broker-connector immediately prior to or during the market open incident.

inferences.statement: The order failures at market open were directly caused by upstream broker-api HTTP 429 rate limit responses rather than database saturation or connection pool starvation.
The database CPU spike at 03:45 UTC was driven by app-open user traffic triggering unindexed queries on the holdings table rather than order processing traffic.

assumptions.statement: Broker-connector does not currently implement a local token-bucket rate limiter or request smoothing queue to throttle order bursts below 300 req/s.

timeline.event: NSE/BSE market opens. Order submission traffic and portfolio open traffic surge.
broker-connector logs first HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response from broker-api citing a limit of 300 req/s.
order-service logs first rejected customer order with HTTP 503 after exhausting 2 retries following broker rate limit 429.
order-service error rate rises to ~15.5% and broker-connector error rate rises to ~11.3%; database slow queries increase to 16-37/min.
order-service error rate peaks at 15.62%.
Trading desk lead reports INC-4849 suspecting order-service and database.
broker-connector records final sampled 429 response from broker-api.
order-service error rate returns to baseline (~0.29%) as order traffic subsides below broker quota.
Database CPU utilization and slow query counts normalize back to baseline.

confidence.rationale: Direct and sampled error logs explicitly confirm broker-api returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (300 req/s limit) leading directly to order-service HTTP 503 rejections. Clear metrics contradict the reporter's hypothesis of database connection pool or lock contention causing order rejections.

gaps.description: Specific request throughput (req/s) timeseries on broker-connector outbound endpoints was not queried prior to budget limit.
gaps.impact: Minimal; the 429 log messages explicitly indicate the 300 req/s quota was exceeded.

recommendedActions.action: Implement client-side rate limiting and request smoothing (token bucket / leaky bucket) in broker-connector capped at 280-290 req/s, queuing bursts rather than sending them immediately to broker-api.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents market-open order spikes from overwhelming upstream broker-api and receiving 429 rejections.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate a burst of 400 orders/sec in staging and confirm orders are queued and dispatched under 300 req/s without 429 errors.

recommendedActions.action: Renegotiate or request an increased market-open API rate limit with broker-api partner to accommodate opening order volume.
recommendedActions.rationale: A 300 req/s quota is insufficient for peak market-open volume during high-volatility sessions.
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm updated contract or API gateway quota configuration with broker provider.

recommendedActions.action: Add an index on holdings(user_id, updated_at) to resolve the slow queries causing the secondary database CPU spike at market open.
recommendedActions.rationale: Repeated queries took up to 3.2s, driving DB CPU to 77% during the morning peak.
recommendedActions.verification: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on 'SELECT ... FROM holdings WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY updated_at' and verify index scan with execution under 5 ms.

# Investigation report: Orders erroring at the open

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.88 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
At market open (09:15 IST / 03:45 UTC on 2026-09-14), stock orders experienced a ~15.5% failure rate lasting until ~04:21 UTC (09:51 IST). Concurrently, primary database CPU spiked from ~35% to ~77%. Investigation confirmed that order rejections were directly caused by upstream broker API rate limiting (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests due to exceeding the 300 req/s threshold), which caused order-service to exhaust its retries and return HTTP 503. The concurrent database CPU spike was an independent side effect of market-open portfolio traffic running unindexed holdings queries and did not cause database pool exhaustion or order timeouts.

**Root cause:** Surging market-open order placement traffic exceeded upstream broker-api's rate limit quota of 300 requests/second. Upstream broker-api responded with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests), causing broker-connector to fail order submissions and order-service to exhaust its retry budget, rejecting approximately 15% of customer orders with HTTP 503.

## Hypotheses
1. **Market-open order volume exceeded the external broker API rate limit of 300 req/s. Upstream broker-api returned HTTP 429 responses to broker-connector, causing order-service to exhaust retries and reject orders with HTTP 503.** — `broker-connector`, rate_limiting_or_quota, confidence 0.88, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_7, ev_8, ev_15, ev_17, ev_18] · Contradicting: none
   - Direct error logs in broker-connector and order-service demonstrate repeated HTTP 429 responses from broker-api citing a 300 req/s limit starting at 03:45:05 UTC, exactly coinciding with the surge in error rates across both services until 04:21 UTC.
2. **Market-open user traffic triggered unindexed holdings queries on database, saturating database CPU to ~77% and degrading order-service database transactions.** — `database`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.12, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_2, ev_3, ev_5, ev_13, ev_16] · Contradicting: [ev_6, ev_11, ev_14, ev_15, ev_17]
   - Although database CPU spiked to ~77% due to slow queries on the holdings table, database connection pool wait times in order-service remained minimal (peaking at only 5.14 ms), lock wait times remained steady (~4 ms), and order-service logs contained zero database timeout or connection exhaustion errors.

## Facts
- order-service error_rate jumped from a baseline of ~0.3-0.5% to ~15.5% between 03:46 UTC and 04:17 UTC (peaking at 15.62% at 04:03 UTC) before returning to baseline by 04:21 UTC. [ev_8]
- broker-connector error_rate spiked from ~0.2% to ~11.3% between 03:46 UTC and 04:17 UTC (peaking at 11.34% at 03:48 UTC) before returning to baseline by 04:21 UTC. [ev_7]
- broker-connector logged 378 occurrences of 'POST /orders -> 429 Too Many Requests (limit 300 req/s; retry-after 1s)' from upstream broker-api between 03:45:05 UTC and 04:20:59 UTC. [ev_15, ev_18]
- order-service logged 290 occurrences of 'order <ref> rejected: broker rate limit (429) after 2 retries' returning status 503 between 03:45:32 UTC and 04:21:29 UTC. [ev_15, ev_17, ev_18]
- order-service db_pool_wait_ms remained between 2.2 ms and 5.14 ms throughout the window. [ev_6]
- Database db_lock_wait_ms remained between 3.5 ms and 4.5 ms and active_connections remained steady around ~175 connections without connection spikes. [ev_9, ev_11]
- Database cpu_utilization jumped from ~35% to 50.37% at 03:45 UTC and remained elevated at 72-77% until ~04:30 UTC, coinciding with slow queries (1100-3200 ms) executing 'SELECT ... FROM holdings WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY updated_at'. [ev_1, ev_3, ev_13]
- No deployments, migrations, or config changes occurred on order-service, database, or broker-connector immediately prior to or during the market open incident. [ev_4, ev_10, ev_12]

## Inferences
- The order failures at market open were directly caused by upstream broker-api HTTP 429 rate limit responses rather than database saturation or connection pool starvation. [ev_5, ev_6, ev_7, ev_8, ev_15, ev_17, ev_18]
- The database CPU spike at 03:45 UTC was driven by app-open user traffic triggering unindexed queries on the holdings table rather than order processing traffic. [ev_1, ev_3, ev_13, ev_17]

## Assumptions
- Broker-connector does not currently implement a local token-bucket rate limiter or request smoothing queue to throttle order bursts below 300 req/s.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-14 09:15:00 IST (03:45:00 UTC)** NSE/BSE market opens. Order submission traffic and portfolio open traffic surge. [ev_3, ev_5]
- **2026-09-14 09:15:05 IST (03:45:05 UTC)** broker-connector logs first HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response from broker-api citing a limit of 300 req/s. [ev_15, ev_18]
- **2026-09-14 09:15:32 IST (03:45:32 UTC)** order-service logs first rejected customer order with HTTP 503 after exhausting 2 retries following broker rate limit 429. [ev_15, ev_17]
- **2026-09-14 09:16:00 IST (03:46:00 UTC)** order-service error rate rises to ~15.5% and broker-connector error rate rises to ~11.3%; database slow queries increase to 16-37/min. [ev_1, ev_7, ev_8, ev_13]
- **2026-09-14 09:33:00 IST (04:03:00 UTC)** order-service error rate peaks at 15.62%. [ev_8]
- **2026-09-14 09:40:00 IST (04:10:00 UTC)** Trading desk lead reports INC-4849 suspecting order-service and database. [ev_8]
- **2026-09-14 09:50:59 IST (04:20:59 UTC)** broker-connector records final sampled 429 response from broker-api. [ev_15]
- **2026-09-14 09:51:29 IST (04:21:29 UTC)** order-service error rate returns to baseline (~0.29%) as order traffic subsides below broker quota. [ev_8, ev_15]
- **2026-09-14 10:00:00 IST (04:30:00 UTC)** Database CPU utilization and slow query counts normalize back to baseline. [ev_3, ev_13]

## Confidence
0.88: Direct and sampled error logs explicitly confirm broker-api returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (300 req/s limit) leading directly to order-service HTTP 503 rejections. Clear metrics contradict the reporter's hypothesis of database connection pool or lock contention causing order rejections.

## Gaps
- Specific request throughput (req/s) timeseries on broker-connector outbound endpoints was not queried prior to budget limit. (impact: Minimal; the 429 log messages explicitly indicate the 300 req/s quota was exceeded.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Implement client-side rate limiting and request smoothing (token bucket / leaky bucket) in broker-connector capped at 280-290 req/s, queuing bursts rather than sending them immediately to broker-api. [ev_15, ev_18]
  - Why: Prevents market-open order spikes from overwhelming upstream broker-api and receiving 429 rejections.
  - Verify: Simulate a burst of 400 orders/sec in staging and confirm orders are queued and dispatched under 300 req/s without 429 errors.
- **[next]** Renegotiate or request an increased market-open API rate limit with broker-api partner to accommodate opening order volume. [ev_15, ev_18]
  - Why: A 300 req/s quota is insufficient for peak market-open volume during high-volatility sessions.
  - Verify: Confirm updated contract or API gateway quota configuration with broker provider.
- **[next]** Add an index on holdings(user_id, updated_at) to resolve the slow queries causing the secondary database CPU spike at market open. [ev_1, ev_3, ev_13]
  - Why: Repeated queries took up to 3.2s, driving DB CPU to 77% during the morning peak.
  - Verify: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on 'SELECT ... FROM holdings WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY updated_at' and verify index scan with execution under 5 ms.
